Failure modes / idempotency: re-categorising a statement gives the same category, rule id and reversal link on every line, with an override, profile and firm rule in play (recompute is idempotent). A malformed table is refused at load, naming the problem, so the categoriser never runs on a partial table. External-call timeouts, retries and dead letters: not applicable, because the categoriser makes no external call and has no queue (the evals test's subprocess has timeout=300).

claims.text: Data / migration: the change is additive. v2 is a new table, v1 stays frozen and pinned by hash, and v1 with frozen:false is refused. The evidence file gains a 'lines' key and keeps the old keys. It is reversible: switching CMA_RULESET back to v1 on a statement categorised under v2 equals a fresh v1 run, and pre-provenance (T01) and T02 checkpoints still resume with inferred v1 rule ids. P7: v2 changes only the listed lines and M1-M16 do not move on the committed corpus. Backfill: not applicable, because v2 is not the default and has written no signed pack; the card_settlement edit changes v2's hash only. PII: evidence lines hold id, category, rule_id and reverses only, never descriptions.
claims.proof_cmd: pytest tests/test_rules_v2.py -k 'rollback_to_v1 or evidence_lines_carry_ids_only or p7_v2'; pytest tests/test_rules.py -k 't02_checkpoint or drafted_before_the_ruleset or switching_v1_frozen'; pytest tests/test_p7_history.py

claims.text: Security: there is no new entry point. The only new input is the CMA_RULESET value, which is checked against the RULESETS allow-list, and an unknown id is refused. Tables are validated at load: types, keys, and compile including OverflowError and RecursionError. Payer descriptions are only regex-searched, never interpolated into a command or query. No secrets are in the changed files. No new dependency: unicodedata is stdlib, and the only pyproject change since 43f3e57 is the pytest markers list.
claims.proof_cmd: pytest tests/test_rules.py -k unknown_ruleset; rg -n -i 'api[_-]?key|secret|password|token' src/cma/rules src/cma/categorise.py tests/test_rules_v2.py; git diff 43f3e57 -- pyproject.toml

claims.text: Performance: categorising 10,000 lines under v2 with a profile stays under the 2-second recompute budget. No queries, so N+1 and indexes are not applicable. The evidence 'lines' payload is O(lines) of ids only, and there are no list endpoints (not applicable).

Observability: every evidence record names the ruleset id and hash and each line's rule_id, including the conflict form with its candidates, so a run proves which table and rule categorised each line. The evals summary names the ruleset. No remote alert, by design (design Observability: nothing leaves the machine); the failure that matters, a bad table, fails closed at load with a non-zero exit and no evidence written (test_cma_run_refuses_a_changed_v1_and_writes_no_evidence).
claims.proof_output: both pass within the 688 suite run; record['ruleset'] == {'id': 'v2', 'sha256': ...}; per-line rule ids asserted

notes:
Hardener change: v2's card_settlement rule (v1's synthetic acquirer wording ACQUIRER SETTLEMENT / PAYGATE PAYOUT / CARD SETTLEMENT) was a bare regex with no word edges, so a Unicode letter glued to it (CAFÉACQUIRER SETTLEMENT) still counted as trading receipts. This is the same class as verify-32 finding 3. It is now a names list (same words, same rule id), with test_p_r4_v1_acquirer_wording_is_whole_words_in_any_script_too. v1 is untouched; v2's hash changes (no signed pack exists).

Gaps for the owner (not changed; each is a design or scope call):
(1) The remaining regex-pattern rules in v2 do not fully follow design C1's 'whole words in any script'. invoice_transfer has a Unicode-aware leading \b but no trailing edge, so 'INV 12É' or 'INV 123A' still matches; adding an edge would stop letter-suffixed invoice refs from matching, which is a behaviour call. loan_drawdown and loan_repayment ('\bLOAN\b|FINANCE\b') have no leading edge on FINANCE, so 'REFINANCE LTD' is a loan drawdown. That is non-trading and can only lower M2. The debit-only patterns (hmrc_vat, hmrc_paye, owner_drawings, bank_fees, payroll) are v1 wording. A decision is needed on whether C1's whole-word rule covers pattern rules too.
(2) No remote alerting, by design (local-first); the fail-closed table load stands in for an alert. No runbook entry beyond the README rollback line.
(3) No changelog file exists in the repo, so no release-note line was written; the README is the user-facing note.
(4) The judgement queue is R15/T21 per D60 and was deliberately not built here.
(5) The changes are left uncommitted in the worktree for the pipeline to commit.
